sections.h2: Can a Paterson house be sold without waiting on a listing?
sections.html:
A cash offer on a house left in its current state skips repairs and showings, while a listing or direct sale takes more time. Paterson adds its own layers for vacant buildings, rent leveling and certificates of occupancy, so learn which apply before you choose a route.

Paterson serves as Passaic County's seat and its largest municipality, home to 161,793 people in the 2025 Census estimate and spread over 8.41 square miles of land. Owners live in just 26.9 percent of its homes, so sellers often hold small rental buildings or inherited the property. Start with this checklist:

  • Confirm whether the property counts as vacant, which triggers a city registration.
  • Find out if tenants live there and whether the building is covered by the rent leveling ordinance.
  • Collect the deed, the payoff figure and any code violation notices.
  • Ask the Division of Community Improvements what inspection a change of occupancy needs.

sections.h2: What is Paterson like for people selling a home?
sections.html:
Paterson was founded in 1791 by the Society for Establishing Useful Manufactures, which wanted to run mills off the Great Falls of the Passaic River. The first plans came from Pierre L'Enfant. The city grew into Silk City in the 19th century, and after a fire in 1902 downtown was rebuilt with four to seven story Beaux-Arts buildings, including City Hall from 1894. Today the Great Falls are part of the national park system, and the Paterson Museum sits in the Great Falls Historic District.

Paterson City Hall dates to 1894 and was designed by the New York firm Carrere and Hastings after the Hotel de Ville in Lyon, the silk capital of Europe. The Passaic County Courthouse Annex stands in the same downtown. Paterson's Farmers Market operates in the Lakeview section, and many North Jersey shoppers drive in for produce. The Passaic River winds northeast past Totowa into Paterson, then turns south toward the city of Passaic and Newark, which is why riverside lots deserve a close look at the flood map.

Parks include Eastside, Westside and Pennington Parks, and Lambert Castle, built in 1892 for a silk mill owner, is a local landmark. Neighborhood character changes quickly from ward to ward. The Eastside and the Manor Section are in the 3rd Ward, Hillcrest is a largely residential area west of downtown, Lakeview sits in the south near the farmers market, and People's Park centers on Twenty-First Avenue. South Paterson is home to large Turkish and Arab communities.

Interstate 80 runs through the city, and State Routes 4, 19 and 20 serve it, with the Garden State Parkway crossing the south end. NJ Transit's Main Line train at Paterson station goes to Hoboken Terminal with a connection at Secaucus Junction, and the Broadway Bus Terminal in downtown is the end of many bus lines. Paterson Public Schools operate 43 schools with 24,692 students in 2023-24.

In August 2011 Hurricane Irene sent the Passaic River up to levels unseen in about a century, displacing thousands of people and closing river bridges. Anyone selling a riverside house should prepare an honest flood answer for the buyer.

sections.h2: How does the Census describe Paterson's housing?
sections.html:
Renters hold most of the housing here, and the median owned home is valued near $360,000. These Census Bureau QuickFacts cover the city as a whole.

sections.h2: Which Paterson city rules should a seller know?
sections.html:
Building, electrical, plumbing and fire inspectors enforce the state construction code in Paterson. They issue permits and final approvals, including Certificates of Occupancy and Continued Certificates of Occupancy. Inspections, licenses, permits and certificates of occupancy run through the Division of Community Improvements, and its construction code page posts weekday hours, mornings through late afternoon. The city's posted number for that division is 973-321-1232, so call for what a sale requires.

  • Vacant buildings: an owner must register a vacant building within 30 days of it becoming vacant or of taking ownership, and the annual registration fee is $2,000. The owner names a local agent aged 21 or older who can be reached at all hours.
  • Foreclosed property: a creditor must register within seven days of starting foreclosure, at $500 a year.
  • Sold or transferred property: once a vacant property is sold or transferred, the owner gives the city proof within 30 days.
  • Rent leveling: owners of covered rentals submit an annual property registration form under Chapter 381 of the municipal code, at no fee, within 30 days of receiving it.

A property can be deemed abandoned in Paterson once it has gone six months without legal occupancy and meets another test: no rehabilitation, stalled construction, an unpaid and delinquent tax installment, or a nuisance finding by the public officer. Inspectors look for signs such as boarded windows, disconnected utilities, piled-up mail and overgrown yards when they decide a building is vacant. Check with the Division of Community Improvements whether your house has been flagged, ahead of any contract.

sections.h2: What state fees and forms apply when a Paterson house sells?
sections.html:
Trenton, not City Hall, sets the Realty Transfer Fee, and the seller pays it. The rates climb in bands from $2.90 up to $6.05 per $500 for prices above $350,000, and from $2.00 up to $3.90 for prices at or below it. The Census median home value of $360,100 sits right above that $350,000 line, so ask your closing attorney for the exact dollar amount.

Sellers who are seniors, blind or disabled pay reduced bands, and the claim is made on a form recorded with the deed. An estate deed to an heir is exempt. A GIT/REP form is recorded too, signed by whoever signs the deed, so the State can tell if a seller from another state must prepay income tax.

Flood answers are required as well. Since March 20, 2024, the disclosure statement has to state the FEMA flood zone and any known flooding before the buyer signs, and the DEP offers a Flood Risk Notification Tool to help.

sections.h2: How can I appeal Paterson property taxes?
sections.html:
Appeals go to the Passaic County Board of Taxation, and the petition must be in its hands by April 1. After a citywide revaluation or reassessment the date is May 1.

The owner must show the assessment misses market value or falls outside the district's common level range, which is 15 percent either side of the average ratio. Property assessed above $1,000,000 can skip to the State Tax Court, and a county board ruling can be taken to that court within 45 days. Your balance comes from the Paterson tax collector.

faqs.q: Must I register a vacant Paterson house?
faqs.a: Yes, when it fits the city's definition of a vacant building. Registration is due within 30 days, with a $2,000 yearly fee.

faqs.q: How does Paterson treat foreclosed properties?
faqs.a: The creditor that files the foreclosure complaint registers the property within seven days, at $500 for the first year and each renewal.

faqs.q: Which office issues certificates of occupancy in Paterson?
faqs.a: The Division of Community Improvements, which enforces the Uniform Construction Code. The city's construction code page posts weekday office hours.

faqs.q: Does the seller cover the state transfer fee in Paterson?
faqs.a: Yes. The State bills the seller at recording, in bands that rise with the price.

faqs.q: What is the Paterson tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: April 1, or May 1 after a revaluation, at the Passaic County Board of Taxation.
